M.V.Cherian, Koovamattom, Velloor, Kottayam 2. T.C.John, Terthikkattu, Aymanam, Kottayam. By Adv. Sri.S.Gopakumaran Nair (Sr.) Respondents/Respondents/Complainant And State:-: -------------------------------------------- 1. C.V.Abdul Jaleel Food Inspector, Kottayam Municipality. 2. State, Represented By The Public Prosecutor, High Court Of Kerala, Ernakulam R2 By Public Prosecutor Sri.R.Githesh This Criminal Revision Petition Having Been Finally Heard On 11-01-2016, The Court On The Same Day Passed The Following: Scl. M.V.Cherian vs C.V.Abdul Jaleel on 11 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40616643/ 1 B. Sudheendra Kumar, J. ------------------------------------- Crl.R.P. No. 2675 of 2003 -------------------------------------- Dated this the 11th day of January, 2016 Order
texts.facts: 2. Heard. 3. The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 18.11.1996 at about 10.45 a.m., PW1, the Food Inspector purchased 750 ml. of cow curd from the first accused. The second accused was the licencee of the said restaurant. After taking the sample as per law, one of the samples was sent to the Public Analyst. The public analyst submitted Ext.P11 report stating that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for cow curd. Thereafter, the complaint was filed before the trial court. The trial court framed a charge and proceeded with the case. While so, Ext.P13 report from the Central Food Laboratory was received. The trial court considered the report of the Central Food Laboratory and convicted the revision petitioners. Ext.P13 report would also show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for cow curd. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW3 were examined and Exts.P1 to P18 were marked for the prosecution. No evidence was adduced on the side of the revision petitioners.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioners has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P13 report cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated. the revision petitioners relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. A Division Bench of this Court in judgment dated 17-11-2015 in Crl.M.C. No. 417 of 2011 held that the decision in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) is applicable to all cases.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioners has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext.
